item.title: Reference stays attached to code
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: How Ze builds its command reference from the binary, and why generated pages still need human judgement.

item.title: AI coding has not had its Rails moment
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Rails gave developers and tools a shared project layout. AI coding needs a comparable convention for finding the decisions and evidence that each project must supply for itself.

item.title: The repository is half the AI harness
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: A plugin change shows how Ze routes an AI agent from a task index to a rule, an implementation and a rejecting check, and what happens when those checks are wrong.

item.title: The proof is the expensive part
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Following one malformed BGP attribute from the RFC through Ze's tests to its public evidence shows where the proof stops and what still needs human judgement.

item.title: How Ze reuses memory for BGP UPDATEs
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Following one BGP UPDATE through receive-buffer reuse, borrowed views, long-lived attributes and independently owned peer output.

item.title: One BGP UPDATE, many peers
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: How Ze finishes each peer's policy decision before reusing a matching UPDATE-body rebuild, with separate ownership for each rebuilt send.

item.title: AI slop is the wrong test
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze is an AI-written network operating system. I remain responsible for what it ships, including the mistakes a model makes and the limits of the tests meant to catch them.
